newsitem.title: SWEDEN: RALLYING-MCRAE TAKES ADVANTAGE OF ERIKSSON'S GEARBOX PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-MCRAE TAKES ADVANTAGE OF ERIKSSON'S GEARBOX PROBLEMS.

text.p: Colin McRae overtook Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson to lead the Swedish rally on Sunday after his Subaru team mate encountered gearbox problems.

Eriksson maintained his overnight seven seconds advantage over the Scotsman up to the start of the 35-km long 12th stage but, with his car jumping out of sixth gear, he managed only to set the fourth best time and dropped eight seconds behind.
"It is only a minor problem but it makes a difference on the very long stages," said Eriksson, who dropped a further second behind on the 13th stage.
Spaniard Carlos Sainz, in a Ford, remained in third place after the morning stages ahead Swede Tomas Radstrom in a Toyota.
Reigning world champion Tommi Makinen of Finland retained fifth place following the one minute 20 seconds penalty he incurred for a late check out from Saturday's service point in Borlange.
The unseasonal Swedish weather continued to provide worries for the drivers with rain throughout the morning turning the snow stages to slush and raising fears among the teams about aquaplaning.
